- fix: Rename .js files to .mjs. Otherwise Lambda can't find the handler for execution
- fix: The Lambda handler must be async even if the function itself doesn't use it. Otherwise Lambda always returns "null"
- fix: Parse the input JSON body for the Lambda function only if it is a string. It is already an object when using tests in the Lambda console.
- Extract the core logic in the Lambda function to a separate function --> enable (local) tests
- --> Lambda functions can now be executed via the AWS console and test events
- Package the code for the Lambda functions based on the subdir names in the build dir --> avoid hardcoded names
- Update job name for the backend and infrastructure deployment in the CircleCI pipeline to make the name more understandable
- Add config file for prettier to increase max line length

author: ekzhu
body:
Resolves #3946


Usage

```python
from autogen_ext.models import OpenAIChatCompletionClient
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent, Handoff
from autogen_agentchat.teams import Swarm
from autogen_agentchat.task import MaxMessageTermination

model_client = OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-4o")

agent1 = AssistantAgent(
    "Alice",
    model_client=model_client,
    handoffs=["Bob"],
    system_message="You are Alice and you only answer questions about yourself.",
)
agent2 = AssistantAgent(
    "Bob", model_client=model_client, system_message="You are Bob and your birthday is on 1st January."
)

team = Swarm([agent1, agent2])
await team.run("What is bob's birthday?", termination_condition=MaxMessageTermination(3))
```

Alternatively, you can use `Handoff` for more detailed specification:
```python
agent1 = AssistantAgent(
    "Alice",
    model_client=model_client,
    handoffs=[Handoff(target="Bob", description="Handoff the conversation to bob", name="transfer_to_bob", message="Conversation transferred to Bob, adopt Bob's persona immediately")],
    system_message="You are Alice and you only answer questions about yourself.",
)
```

body:
Jeg har laget en ny komponent for å håndtere en type accordion-funksjon vi manglet. Dette er en "grupperings-komponent" for den gamle `nve-accordion` som sørger for at kun ett element kan være åpent om gangen. Tanken er å slippe å skrive spesialkode for dette, slik det er beskrevet i https://shoelace.style/components/details#grouping-details
Se også denne: https://github.com/shoelace-style/shoelace/discussions/1638

Den nye grupperinsg-komponenten har fått navnet `nve-accordion` og jeg har endret navnet på den gamle `nve-accordion` til `nve-accordion-item` ~~`nve-details`, siden komponenten arver fra heter `sl-details`~~. Jeg syntes navnet `nve-accordion` passet bedre på selve grupperings-komponenten.
Å bytte ut implementasjonen av en komponent er jo et ganske kraftig brudd på grensesnittet, så jeg jekket opp versjonsnummeret til 0.4.0.

Vet du var litt skeptisk til en slik løsning, @tomapedersen, så kom gjerne tilbakemeldinger på om du tror det kan funke og evt. hva som må til for at dette skal bli bra nok.

Jeg har testet det kjapt i Vue, og det ser ut som det funker.

Jeg har også tatt inn forslagene i #313 her, så vi slipper evt. konflikter.

body:
## Description # Pull Request Justification for Level 3 Review ## Overview This pull request introduces several significant enhancements to the cart functionality of our application. The changes aim to improve type safety, dynamic data handling, and overall user experience when interacting with the cart and wishlist. Below are the detailed justifications for this PR. --- ### level2 (20-25points) ## 1. Backend Enhancements ### Added Necessary Backend Actions - **Type Safety**: Implemented backend actions with TypeScript for fetching cart queries, ensuring robust type safety throughout the application. - **Globalized Cart State**: The cart state has been globalized via the CartProvider, allowing seamless access across different components in the application. This enhances maintainability and reduces redundancy. ### Benefits of Type Safety and Global State - **Consistency**: Type safety reduces the likelihood of runtime errors and improves code readability, making it easier for other developers to understand and maintain the code. - **Ease of Use**: Developers can now access the cart state from any component that subscribes to the CartProvider, streamlining the development process. - **Reduced Boilerplate**: Global state management minimizes the need for prop drilling, allowing components to focus on their primary responsibilities. --- ## 2. Dynamic Data Handling ### Replaced Hardcoded Data - **Dynamic User Cart**: Removed hardcoded data from the cart and implemented logic to fetch the user's cart directly from the database. This ensures that users always see their current cart contents. - **Updated Cart Card Design**: Modified the cart card to accommodate detailed product information, improving the overall UI and providing users with necessary information at a glance. ### Enhanced User Experience - **Real-Time Updates**: By fetching cart data from the database, users can experience real-time updates to their cart. - **Improved Usability**: Displaying detailed product information in the cart card enhances user experience by providing critical information like price and images. ### Dynamic Cart Summary - **Cart Summary Behavior**: The behavior of the cart summary has been made dynamic, reflecting the actual products in the cart. This ensures users are accurately informed of their cart contents and total price, enhancing overall usability. --- ###level2 (20-25 points) ## 3. Wishlist Integration ### Implemented Add to Cart Functionality in Wishlist - **Duplication Prevention**: The add-to-cart functionality in the wishlist is now smartly designed to prevent users from adding the same item to the cart multiple times. This feature enhances user experience by avoiding confusion and maintaining a clean cart. ### Benefits of Wishlist Integration - **Streamlined User Workflow**: Users can quickly move items from their wishlist to the cart, creating a seamless shopping experience. - **Reduced User Error**: Preventing duplicacy ensures that users do not mistakenly add the same item multiple times, maintaining clarity in the cart. --- ## 4. Additional Improvements ### Updated Contributing Guidelines - **Minor Changes**: Minor updates to the contributing guidelines have been made to reflect recent changes in project structure and workflows, ensuring clarity for new contributors. ### .env.example File Updates - **Environment Variables**: Adjusted the `.env.example` file to include new environment variables required for the recent changes, ensuring that all developers can set up their environment correctly. --- ## Conclusion The changes introduced in this PR significantly enhance the application's cart and wishlist functionalities. The improvements in type safety, dynamic data handling, and user experience justify the need for a Level 3 review. Some awk comments are not highlighted. The following is valid awk:
```awk
{ # Comment
    for (i = 0; # BAD
        i < 1; # BAD
        i++) # Comment
    { # Comment
        print # Comment
    } # Comment
} # Comment
```
In vim, the two comments `# BAD` are not currently highlighted. This fixes that issue.

author: shimmeringtrashpile
body:
Created a `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` file that creates a GitHub Action

This action does the following.

Upon push to the main branch:
The GitHub Action provisions an ubuntu-latest and runs a job on it that:

- Checks out the main branch.
- SSHes into our staging server with our SSL key.
- Once logged in...
    1. changes directory to /home/nmcdev/nmc-website
    2. pulls the latest nmc-website **main** branch to the staging server
    3. runs `docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build` to build new docker images and start them.

This is currently untested, so we'll see what happens when I try to run it!

body:
This pull request includes several updates across the backend and frontend components of the TimeManager project, focusing on new functionalities, code refactoring, and UI improvements. The most important changes include adding a new endpoint to fetch contract time by user ID, updating the frontend to use new icons, and refactoring some Vue components for better state management.

### Backend Changes:
* **New Endpoint Addition:**
  * Updated the router to include the new endpoint (`backend/lib/time_manager_web/router.ex`).

### Frontend Changes:
* **Component Updates:**
  * Refactored `BalanceComponent.vue` to simplify state management and calculations for work percentages (`frontend/src/components/Balance/BalanceComponent.vue`).
  * Updated `SummaryCard.vue` to replace font icons with SVG icons and adjusted the layout for better visual hierarchy (`frontend/src/components/Card/SummaryCard/SummaryCard.vue`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb488d6d28054265848903118ef0a0e9e6d917c8955ff36f61e450a49f4f582eL13-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cb488d6d28054265848903118ef0a0e9e6d917c8955ff36f61e450a49f4f582eL22-R44) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cb488d6d28054265848903118ef0a0e9e6d917c8955ff36f61e450a49f4f582eL71-R105) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cb488d6d28054265848903118ef0a0e9e6d917c8955ff36f61e450a49f4f582eL106-R134) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-cb488d6d28054265848903118ef0a0e9e6d917c8955ff36f61e450a49f4f582eL128-R144)

* **Settings Page Enhancements:**
  * Modified `SettingsDocuments.vue` to dynamically fetch and display contract details based on the authenticated user (`frontend/src/pages/Settings/SettingsDocuments.vue`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-78c5aea44bb1c21ddfcc997d64843e476b9f983f6300bad30745c302a9bd1b59L72-R73) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-78c5aea44bb1c21ddfcc997d64843e476b9f983f6300bad30745c302a9bd1b59L82-R109)
